design:
BEFORE looking at the attack windows:
  A  transferred: 2015 calibration unchanged. Trailing references need 1.5 h
     of data plus a 1 h lag, so the drifting checks only start at ~12:35.
  B  recalibrated on this plant: calibrate on 10:05-11:15, measure false
     alarms on 11:15-12:30 and 13:30-13:45. Within 3.7 h there is no membrane
     drift to track, so all six checks use fixed medians. Same 1.2 x worst
     rule, same steady-state and flow gates, same 10 s persistence.
  Scoring: hit = any alarm inside a burst window [start, start+3 min).
  Alarms in the 10 min "sleep" after each burst are reported separately,
  since a disruption can outlast its burst.

diagnosis_after_scoring.verdict: Not a valid test of RO-stage detection. The disruption bursts switched UF/backwash and upstream actuators (MV301, MV303, P301, P602, P101, P201, P203; P3_STATE sequence changes) and left stages P4-P5 unchanged (P4_STATE, P5_STATE constant). The RO-stage alarms in both variants come from slow drift, not the attack: the plant was still settling after start-up (feed conductivity AIT503 rose 29 -> 46 uS/cm over ~90 min; RO-feed ORP AIT502 drifted 190 -> 207 mV all session).
what_it_does_show: The two pure identities (flow balance, feed meters) transferred from 2015 to a reconfigured 2019 plant (recirculation off, feed conductivity 45 vs 268 uS/cm) with no alarm at any point in A6.

Ratio and ORP checks need settled-plant calibration over hours; a 3.7 h recording that starts at plant start-up cannot support them. Variant B (calibrated on 70 min of start-up) false-alarmed on 84% of its test window.
AIT402 reads 195.05 mV +/- 0.05 all session: likely a stuck sensor, which the current checks do not flag as such.
diagnosis_after_scoring.note: Diagnosis done after the pre-registered scoring; the scores above are left as recorded.
